docs.text: Retrieval augmented generation connects a vector index with a language model so the model can answer questions using your private documents.
A reranker reorders the top retrieved passages with a cross encoder to boost answer relevance.
The crawler fetches web pages while obeying robots.txt and a per host rate limit so it ingests sites politely.
OIDC lets users log in through an external identity system; it checks a JWT signature against a JWKS public key for enterprise access control.
Role based access control assigns each API key a role such as admin or user, and the audit log records every request.
Prometheus metrics and health endpoints let operators watch the service and connect Grafana dashboards.
You can swap the language model or embedding backend; OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and built in fakes are supported.
The offline evaluation harness measures recall, precision, and mean reciprocal rank to track retrieval quality.
Incremental crawling uses entity tags and last modified headers to skip pages that have not changed since the last visit.
Documents are split into overlapping chunks before embedding so each passage fits the model context.
The Qdrant vector database can store embeddings at scale instead of the in memory store.
The command line tool can serve the API, ingest a URL, crawl a site, and run a search without writing code.
Multiple pages are fetched at once with a bounded worker pool to speed up large crawls.
Every authenticated request is written to an append only audit file for compliance and forensics.
The hosted query console shows retrieved passages together with clickable source links, so a visitor needs no installed software.
When the service is healthy it returns a 200 on the live probe and a 503 with no details on the ready probe.
